review.summary: Based on the plan text supplied, WP-04 does not block the unavailable branch of WP-12. The only link between them is the shared-writer rule, which orders who writes the electronic-invoice scheduler files (WP-04 first, then WP-12) and forbids actually running billing cycles. That ordering only matters when WP-12 touches those files, which happens only in the adapter (automatic issuance) branch. The owner chose the unavailable branch, and the evidence shows no scheduler, adapter, schema, payment-flow or provider-send changes. That branch's acceptance requires an explicit 'unavailable' message and no claim of issuance. Its validation path is targeted presentation tests plus an independent Billing review. The four file hashes match the snapshot, assess_acceptance is READY, and a qualified critical review was observed, so this evidence meets those requirements. WP-12 can complete on the unavailable branch if two things stay true: no automated issuance exists, and the WP-04 -> WP-12 scheduler handoff comes back into force for any future adapter or provider enablement, which must go through a new reviewed change. That WP-04's scheduler is incomplete and the Preview deployments were removed does not change this. I found no blockers or major issues. The two minor findings below are about recording the decision clearly and avoiding a risk if a provider is enabled later. Neither one blocks delivery.

findings.file: Goal Plan – WP-12 completion / dependency record
findings.area: WP-12 closure note and the WP-04 -> WP-12 shared-writer rule
findings.issue: Closing WP-12 on the unavailable branch while WP-04 is incomplete depends on reading the shared-writer dependency as applying only to the adapter branch. The supplied evidence does not show that reading, or the conditions behind it, written into the plan or closure record.
findings.evidence: The shared-writer rule assigns the electronic-invoice scheduler files WP-04 -> WP-12. The WP-12 scope offers either an adapter OR an unavailable presentation. The owner decision selects 'not yet available'. WP-04's scheduler is incomplete. The current evidence states that no scheduler or adapter files were changed.
findings.impact: Without a written condition, a later reader could take WP-12 as fully done and enable a provider, or finish WP-04's scheduler, without the WP-04 -> WP-12 handoff or a Billing review. That would break the 'future enablement requires a new reviewed change' requirement.
findings.recommended_fix: In the WP-12 closure record, state that: (1) WP-12 is closed on the unavailable branch only; (2) the WP-04 dependency did not apply because no scheduler, adapter or provider files were touched; (3) any adapter, scheduler or provider enablement is out of scope and needs a new work package that goes through the WP-04 -> WP-12 handoff, Sandbox issuance/retry/writeback tests and an independent Billing review; (4) no automated issuance and no tax-exemption claim exist.
findings.required_test: Documentation check: the closure record contains the conditional statement above. Confirm the changed-file list for WP-12 contains no scheduler, adapter, schema or payment-flow paths.

findings.file: Merchant invoice UI / checkout invoice-request handling (queued state)
findings.issue: Requests are stored as 'queued' (recorded, not issued). If a provider or the WP-04 scheduler is enabled later, these stored requests could be picked up and issued automatically without anyone deciding to do so.
findings.evidence: Current evidence: 'queued means request recorded/not issued; historical records remain visible.' WP-04's scheduler is incomplete and will eventually hand off to WP-12 under the shared-writer rule.
findings.impact: A future change could issue invoices for old requests that were never reviewed, possibly with stale buyer or tax details. The checks in this change do not cover that, though it does not affect what the current branch delivers.
findings.recommended_fix: No change to the current product code is needed. Add a requirement to the future-enablement work package: the processing of existing 'queued' records (issue, expire or ask the merchant to confirm) must be an explicit decision covered by that change's Billing review.
findings.required_test: In the future adapter work package: an integration test showing that existing 'queued' records are handled only by the explicitly reviewed backlog policy. Nothing new is needed for the current change.
